node.title: Re: -T changed behavior
node.author: kcott
node.doctext:
G'day [id://1215021|tothestars],

Welcome to the Monastery.

[Please put code, data, program output, and similar text within ... tags. This has a number of benefits: your posts will be easier to read; you won't need to escape special HTML characters (e.g. turn '<' into '<'); it provides a download facility so we can get a verbatim copy of your code.]

You can find the Perl deltas in the [http://perldoc.perl.org/perl.html#Miscellaneous|Miscellaneous section of perldoc]. Looking in [http://perldoc.perl.org/perl5220delta.html#Selected-Bug-Fixes|perl5220delta: Selected Bug Fixes], there's a reference to '-T' that may be what you're looking for. There's another in the [http://perldoc.perl.org/perl5220delta.html#Performance-Enhancements|Performance Enhancements section] but that doesn't look relevant to me. If those don't help, try other deltas in the version range you specified.

You might also want to try:

$ file spk_pre_180208_180715_180419_bpo12_p.bsp

How does the output from that compare with what '-T' is telling you?

I don't have any of those Perl versions handy so I can't do any direct testing for you.

— Ken
